Tips for getting into hospitals 

Get Certifications: If you don't have a degree, earning certifications can help you stand out. Certifications like CHAA (Certified Healthcare Access Associate), CHAM (Certified Healthcare Access Manager), or CRCP (Certified Revenue Cycle Professional) are valuable in healthcare administration. These show employers you have specialized knowledge and are committed to the field.

Start in Patient Access or Patient Financial Services: These entry-level positions are easier to break into, even without extensive healthcare experience. Roles like Patient Access Representative, Financial Counselor, or Insurance Verification Specialist provide foundational knowledge in healthcare operations and are excellent starting points.

Look for Administrative Fellowships: Many hospitals offer administrative fellowship programs for those looking to gain leadership experience in healthcare. These fellowships are excellent opportunities to fast-track your career, giving you hands-on experience and mentorship in various departments.

Leverage Your Network: Networking within healthcare settings, joining professional organizations like NAHAM (National Association of Healthcare Access Management), and attending industry events or webinars can expose you to opportunities and mentors.

Build Your Resume with Experience: Volunteer, intern, or take on part-time roles to get your foot in the door. Any experience in customer service or administrative roles translates well to healthcare administration positions.

Prepare for Revenue Cycle Exams: If you're studying for exams like CHAA, CHAM, or CRCP, check out resources and coaching from experts. Follow my channel @DropPetals for practice test questions and tutorials to help you pass these exams.
